statements.text: GET /tasks?status=<state> returns only tasks whose Status equals <state>, for each TaskState name (Open, InProgress, Done).
The status match is case-insensitive: GET /tasks?status=open returns the same set as GET /tasks?status=Open.
GET /tasks with an unrecognised status value (e.g. ?status=Bogus) returns HTTP 400 Bad Request and no task list.
GET /tasks with no status parameter returns all tasks, unchanged from the pre-change behaviour.
The other CRUD endpoints (GET /tasks/{id}, POST, PUT, DELETE) are behaviourally unchanged; the 5 baseline integration tests still pass and dotnet build / dotnet test stay green (R-003).
Filtering is implemented at the endpoint/query boundary: Domain/** is unchanged, no domain code references ASP.NET types (R-004), and the TaskState naming is preserved (R-005).
